provenance.notes: Azure Blob Storage (or Azurite), under the Microsoft Customer Agreement and the Product Terms for Azure ('contract'), the content the customer's own. Limits: Microsoft publishes scalability targets, not quotas - 'up to 3,000 requests per second' for a single block blob, 'up to 500' for a page blob (read 2026-11-10, page dated 2026-07-24); past them, and on a hot partition before them, Azure answers 503 Server Busy or 500 Operation Timeout. Per blob, which no scope of the schema counts: unknown (null) here, the figures in this note. The key is the account's (a connection string, an account key or a SAS). Writes and retries: azure-oss/storage-blob's Guzzle middleware retries a request after a 408, 429, 500, 502, 503 or 504 or a timeout, whatever its method. Put Blob, Put Block and Put Block List of the same blob are idempotent (a replay leaves the same blob); a Delete Blob replayed after it succeeded answers 404, nothing is deleted twice; a copy replayed copies the same source onto the same blob.
